title: Smart Helmet with Accident Detection and Emergency Alert
abstract: A smart helmet that detects crashes with an accelerometer, checks that the rider is wearing it before the bike starts, and sends the GPS location to emergency contacts by SMS.
existing: Accident victims often wait a long time for help because nobody informs family or emergency services, and riders frequently start the bike without wearing a helmet.
proposed: An ESP32 reads the MPU6050 for sudden impact and tilt, an IR sensor confirms the helmet is worn, and on a crash the GSM module sends an SMS with a GPS map link. A buzzer gives a short cancel window for false alarms.
advantages: Bike starts only when the helmet is worn

title: IoT Smart Agriculture Monitoring and Automatic Irrigation
abstract: Monitors soil moisture, temperature and humidity, switches the water pump automatically and shows live readings on a cloud dashboard.
existing: Farmers water fields on a fixed schedule or by guesswork, which wastes water and needs someone on site.
proposed: A NodeMCU reads the soil-moisture and DHT11 sensors, runs the pump through a relay when the soil is dry, and uploads readings to a cloud dashboard where the pump can also be switched from a phone.

title: LoRa-Based Long-Range Environmental Monitoring Network
abstract: Low-power sensor nodes send environmental readings several kilometres over LoRa to a gateway that uploads them to the cloud.
existing: Wi-Fi and Bluetooth sensors only reach a few tens of metres, and GSM-based nodes cost more to run and use more power.
proposed: Battery- or solar-powered nodes read a BME280 and transmit over LoRa. An ESP32 gateway receives the packets and pushes them to a cloud dashboard.
advantages: No SIM card or recurring cost per node

title: Line Follower and Obstacle Avoiding Robot
abstract: A two-wheel robot that follows a track with IR sensors and steers around obstacles detected by an ultrasonic sensor.
existing: Simple line followers stop or crash when something blocks the path.
proposed: An Arduino reads an IR sensor array for line position (PID control) and an HC-SR04 for obstacles, and drives two motors through an L298N to follow the line and go around obstacles.

title: Wireless Gesture-Controlled 4-DOF Robotic Arm
abstract: A glove with flex and motion sensors controls a four-axis robotic arm wirelessly.
existing: Robotic arms are usually controlled with joysticks or buttons, which is slow and not intuitive.
proposed: A glove-mounted Arduino reads flex sensors and an MPU6050 and sends the hand position over nRF24L01. The arm-side controller drives four servos through a PCA9685 to copy the hand's movement.

title: Autonomous Indoor Mapping and Navigation Robot using ROS
abstract: A mobile robot that builds a map of a room with LiDAR (SLAM) and drives itself to goals set on the map.
existing: Indoor robots without mapping follow fixed paths or lines and cannot adapt to a new layout.
proposed: A Raspberry Pi running ROS combines RPLiDAR scans with wheel-encoder odometry to build a map (SLAM) and plan paths. An Arduino Mega handles the motor control.
advantages: Map can be saved and reused

title: Custom PCB Design for a Solar IoT Weather Station
abstract: A two-layer PCB designed from schematic to Gerber files for a solar-powered weather station with charging and sensor headers.
existing: Breadboard and jumper-wire prototypes are fragile and unreliable outdoors.
proposed: The full circuit, including solar charging, a 3.3 V regulator, an ESP32 module and sensors, is captured as a schematic, laid out on a two-layer PCB, fabricated, assembled and tested.

title: BLDC Motor Controller PCB with Over-Current Protection
abstract: A three-phase MOSFET-bridge controller board for brushless DC motors with Hall-sensor commutation and current sensing.
existing: Off-the-shelf ESCs are closed boxes. They cannot be studied or tuned, and many have weak protection.
proposed: An STM32 reads the Hall sensors and a current shunt, then drives a three-phase MOSFET bridge through gate drivers. Speed is set by a potentiometer and the board trips on over-current.
advantages: Open design that can be tuned

title: Edge AI Face Recognition Attendance System
abstract: Recognises students' faces on a Raspberry Pi without any cloud service and records attendance with timestamps.
existing: Paper registers and fingerprint scanners are slow, allow proxy attendance, and need physical contact.
proposed: A Pi camera captures faces. The Raspberry Pi detects and recognises them on the device, logs attendance to a database, shows the name on an LCD and flags unknown faces.

title: Driver Drowsiness Detection and Alert on an Edge Device
abstract: Tracks eye closure and yawning in real time and sounds an alarm when the driver shows signs of drowsiness.
existing: Many accidents are caused by tired drivers, and most vehicles have no warning system.
proposed: A camera facing the driver feeds a Raspberry Pi, which computes eye aspect ratio and mouth opening from facial landmarks. Long eye closure or repeated yawning triggers a buzzer and seat vibration.

title: TinyML Voice-Controlled Home Automation on a Microcontroller
abstract: A small neural network on a microcontroller recognises spoken keywords and switches appliances without an internet connection.
existing: Voice assistants send audio to the cloud, need internet and raise privacy concerns.
proposed: An I2S microphone feeds audio to an ESP32-S3 running a quantised keyword-spotting model (Edge Impulse / TensorFlow Lite Micro). Recognised commands switch relays.
advantages: Private: no audio leaves the device

title: FPGA-Based CNN Accelerator for Image Classification
abstract: Implements the convolution layers of a small CNN in FPGA logic to classify images faster than software running on a CPU.
existing: Running CNNs on general-purpose CPUs is slow and power-hungry for embedded vision.
proposed: A pipelined fixed-point convolution engine, pooling and fully connected layers are written in Verilog/HLS. Images arrive over UART and the predicted class is shown on LEDs or a display.

title: Automatic Number Plate Recognition for Smart Parking
abstract: Reads vehicle number plates at the gate, checks them against an allowed list and opens the barrier automatically.
existing: Manual gate entry is slow, needs a guard and keeps no reliable log.
proposed: An IR sensor detects a vehicle and triggers the camera. The Raspberry Pi finds the plate, reads it with OCR, checks it against the database, opens the servo barrier and logs the entry.

title: Computer Vision Fruit Quality Grading and Sorting Conveyor
abstract: A camera above a conveyor grades fruit by colour, size and defects, and a servo arm pushes rejected fruit aside.
existing: Manual sorting is slow, tiring and inconsistent.
proposed: The Raspberry Pi classifies each fruit from the camera image and sends the grade to an Arduino, which runs the conveyor and moves the sorting servo.

title: Real-Time ECG and Heart-Rate Monitoring with Mobile Alert
abstract: Captures ECG signals, filters noise in real time, calculates heart rate and streams the waveform to a mobile app.
existing: Hospital ECG machines are expensive and fixed, so patients cannot be monitored at home.
proposed: An AD8232 front-end picks up the ECG. The ESP32 filters it digitally, detects R-peaks to calculate heart rate, shows the result on an OLED and streams it to a phone over Bluetooth, alerting on abnormal rates.

title: FreeRTOS-Based Industrial Machine Condition Monitoring
abstract: Uses FreeRTOS tasks to monitor vibration, temperature and current on a machine and trips it when limits are crossed.
existing: Machines are inspected manually at intervals, so faults are found late and cause breakdowns.
proposed: An STM32 runs separate FreeRTOS tasks for each sensor, a fault-trip task with guaranteed response time, and a Modbus/CAN task that reports to a supervisor PC.

title: Solar MPPT Charge Controller using Buck Converter
abstract: A buck-converter charge controller that tracks the solar panel's maximum power point to charge a battery efficiently.
existing: PWM charge controllers waste a large part of the panel's power when the panel and battery voltages differ.
proposed: An Arduino measures panel voltage and current and runs the Perturb & Observe MPPT algorithm, adjusting the buck converter's PWM duty cycle. It also protects the battery and shows readings on an LCD.
advantages: More energy harvested than PWM controllers

title: Wireless Power Transfer for Electric Vehicle Charging (Prototype)
abstract: An inductive-coupling prototype that charges a small battery across an air gap and measures efficiency against coil distance.
existing: Plug-in EV charging needs manual connection, and the connectors wear out over time.
proposed: A high-frequency oscillator drives the transmitter coil. The receiver coil, rectifier and regulator charge the battery, and charging voltage and current are measured at different gaps.

title: College Event Management Web Application
abstract: A web app where students register for events, organisers manage participants, and certificates are generated automatically.
existing: Event registration runs on Google Forms and spreadsheets, and certificates are made by hand.
proposed: A React front-end with an Express API and MongoDB handles student and organiser logins, event registration, attendance and automatic PDF certificates.

title: Fake News Detection using Machine Learning and NLP
abstract: Classifies news articles as real or fake using NLP features and compares several machine-learning models.
existing: Fact-checking by hand is slow, and fake news spreads faster than it can be checked.
proposed: Article text is cleaned and converted to TF-IDF features. Logistic Regression, Naive Bayes and Passive-Aggressive models are compared, and the best one is served through a Flask web page.
